findings.claim: The new diagnostic filter does not drop diagnostics about metadata symbols. When a metadata member has no syntax, the new code (FirstOrDefault()/GetPropertyIdentifierLocation) creates the diagnostic with a null location, which becomes Location.None. In ReportIfLocatedInCompilation, `!diagnostic.Location.IsInSource` is then true, so the diagnostic is reported. Example: a referenced generic struct with an unattributed public member makes the consuming project's analyzer report MsgPack004 (an Error per L2) with no location. That contradicts the method's own remarks ('dropped here'), the new README and MsgPack004.md text ('reported by the assembly that defines it'), and L8 (metadata types are not analysed by the consumer). The consumer gets a build-breaking error it cannot fix, not a clean build.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.Req2283MetadataDiagnosticsTests.UnattributedMemberOfReferencedGenericStruct_NotReportedInConsumer. On head it should fail with an unexpected MsgPack004 diagnostic at Location.None.

findings.claim: The reporter names three unguarded `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` sites (reported lines 735, 1009, 1101). The hunks change only two of them: BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull at 985 and MemberNeedsKey at 1077. No hunk touches the region near the first reported site. If an unguarded index remains in GetObjectInfo, a metadata closed generic struct can still throw IndexOutOfRangeException (CS8785/AD0001) on some member shapes.

receipt_plan.detail: grep -n 'DeclaringSyntaxReferences\[0\]' src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs on head. Any remaining hit reachable from GetObjectInfo is unguarded for metadata symbols. Confirm with Req2283ReferencedGenericStructTests using a member shape that reaches that path.
